lessons.explanation: A hard link is another directory entry for the same inode; a symbolic link stores a path resolved during lookup.
lessons.workedExample:
ln source.txt hard.txt
ln -s source.txt soft.txt
ls -li source.txt hard.txt soft.txt
lessons.expectedResult: Hard links share an inode on the same filesystem; a symbolic link has its own inode and target text.
lessons.exercise:
Make a two-column comparison of links and inodes and symbolic links and hard links. Use the example:
ln source.txt hard.txt
ln -s source.txt soft.txt
ls -li source.txt hard.txt soft.txt
For each concept, write what it can establish and one thing it cannot establish.
lessons.knowledgeCheck: How is links and inodes different from symbolic links and hard links, and which evidence separates them?
lessons.answer: The concepts may interact, but they answer different questions. For links and inodes, the example shows: Hard links share an inode on the same filesystem; a symbolic link has its own inode and target text. Use a separate observation to test claims about symbolic links and hard links.
